transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (CTO, MediBridge), Dr. Sara Martin (Data Privacy Lead), Luis Ortega (Security Engineer), Aisha Khan (Legal)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. With me are Priya our SE and Maya from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Good thanks, Jordan here. We appreciate you making time - going to be pretty focused on security and data handling.
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Great, thanks. We'll do a short run-of topics then dive into specifics, please stop me if my lingo is too fast.
[00:18] Dr. Sara Martin: Works for me. We are primarily concerned about PHI retention, PII handling and explicit confirmation that data won't be used to train models.
[00:24] Alex Chen: Understood, that's the main focus. Quick agenda: SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC and SSO, audit logging and retention, encryption (in transit / at rest), KMS options including customer-managed keys, data residency options, and then prompt/content retention and training usage.
[00:38] Luis Ortega: Awesome. Also want to make sure we cover legal - Aisha will chime on contract language for no-training and data-at-rest encryption.

[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Starting with certifications: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we maintain ISO 27001 alignment - i'll share the certificates after the call. Note: our hosted control plane is SOC 2'd, and Dedicated/Private options can be part of contractual controls for data isolation.
[00:58] Alex Chen: Quick note, our SOC 2 report covers the hosted platform operations, change management and incident response - we'll include scope details.
[01:04] Aisha Khan: When you say scope - does it include access control for customer data and encryption key management?
[01:09] Alex Chen: Yes for hosted, but customers who require customer-managed keys or on-prem controls typically go on Private or Dedicated and we add that to contract annex. We'll provide evidence for both.

[01:18] Dr. Sara Martin: About encryption - we need encryption in transit and at rest, and the ability for customer-managed KMS keys. Also need to know how key rotation works.
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. For at-rest we encrypt using AES-256. For hosted we offer BYOK via cloud KMS (customer-managed), and for Dedicated/Private we support HSM integrations and KMS proxies. Key rotation is managed by the customer's KMS; Redwood respects key revocation and will reject decrypt operations if access is revoked.
[01:44] Jordan Lee: OK that's good. Is there an audit trail for key usage?
[01:47] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we emit key access events to audit logs and we can show example log lines - will attach links. Audits include which tenant, operation, timestamp.

[01:56] Luis Ortega: On audit logs - retention windows? We need 3 years for certain artifacts.
[02:00] Maya Lopez: By default logs are retained 90 days in the console; extended retention is an add-on and we can export logs to the customer's S3 or log sink for long-term storage to meet 3-year retention.
[02:10] Luis Ortega: Good. Exporting to our log archive is acceptable.

[02:15] Priya Kapoor: Moving to RBAC and SSO - Redwood supports SAML2 / OIDC SSO and role-based access controls. Admin roles, developer roles and read-only billing roles are configurable. We also support SCIM provision for user sync.
[02:27] Aisha Khan: Can RBAC be scoped down to route-level access? e.g., allow an engineering team to call embeddings but not create new model endpoints?
[02:33] Priya Kapoor: Yes, fine-grained permissions exist in the console - we can lock down route creation and model rollout permissions. We'll send the permissions matrix.

[02:41] Dr. Sara Martin: Now the critical one: prompt and content retention. We need precise defaults and contractual options.
[02:47] Alex Chen: Short answer: default hosted retention is 30 days for prompts and outputs used for debugging and rate-limiting; we offer a "no-retention" mode where customer prompts/outputs are not stored beyond ephemeral caches used for inference and short-term KV cache eviction. For customers needing no retention we recommend Dedicated or Private with contractual data handling clauses.
[03:06] Jordan Lee: When you say "no training" on customer data - we need an explicit statement that Redwood does not use customer data to train models or improve model weights.
[03:14] Alex Chen: Confirmed - Redwood does not use customer prompts, logs or outputs to further train or fine-tune public models. We may use anonymized telemetry for system performance improvements but not to change model behavior. We'll provide the contractual language for that.
[03:26] Dr. Sara Martin: Are there third-party model providers in the stack that might ingest data? e.g., if a model is proxied to an external provider?
[03:33] Priya Kapoor: We have curated model catalog - when using our hosted models we control the runtime. If a customer chooses to call a third-party model (rare), we surface that explicitly and it's disabled by default. For Dedicated/Private you can pin to specific model artifacts and it's contained.

[03:45] Luis Ortega: For PHI specifically, is there an ability to configure redaction or PII scrubbing pre-send?
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: Yes - we have middleware hooks and pre-processing pipelines: you can enable automatic PII token masking or run a redaction step in your client before sending. We can demo a sample lambda that strips or hashes PHI. Also, for production PHI workloads we recommend Private with our HIPAA addendum - we'll include that note.
[04:08] Aisha Khan: Is Redwood willing to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for HIPAA?
[04:12] Alex Chen: We currently offer HIPAA addendum for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private and can discuss scope in legal. We'll add that to next steps.

[04:20] Jordan Lee: On data residency: we need EU-only residency for MediBridge's EU customers, and US-only for certain state-level data. How granular is region pinning?
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: We support region pinning at tenant level: US, EU (Ireland), and APAC regions are available. For hybrid needs we can set routing policies to keep data in region and provide proof of network egress controls.

[04:37] Dr. Sara Martin: Regarding logs and transcripts - do logs ever include prompt text? We need to understand what is logged.
[04:42] Priya Kapoor: By default we log metadata: request IDs, model ids, latency, token counts. Prompt text is stored only when retention is enabled for debugging and it is encrypted and access-controlled. In no-retention customers prompts are not persisted beyond ephemeral GPU/KV cache and are not written to logs.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: That helps. A follow-up: if a support engineer needs to debug a specific conversation, what's the process for retrieving prompt content?
[05:07] Maya Lopez: Support access is strictly audited. For customers on retention mode we require a ticket, customer approval, and we produce a redacted export. We can also do live screen-share debug without exfiltrating data. All support access is logged and alerted.

[05:20] Luis Ortega: How is customer data segregated at rest on shared infra? Multi-tenant encryption keys?
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: We scope keys per-tenant where possible. In hosted mode there are tenant-specific encryption contexts; in Dedicated/Private you can bring your own key or isolate to dedicated GPU pools.

[05:33] Alex Chen: On backup and deletion: we support deletion APIs and have a documented process for data deletion that triggers downstream scrubs. We'll include SLA for deletion and proof of deletion artifacts.

[05:42] Dr. Sara Martin: I want explicit language for contracts stating no training on customer data and no sharing of prompt-output pairs with humans except with approval.
[05:49] Alex Chen: Understood. We'll provide explicit clause language, and our legal can include auditor-friendly wording. We'll flag the human review policy - by default no human review of customer content unless you enable it or submit for a support case with approval.

[06:01] Aisha Khan: Are there cases where human-in-the-loop labeling might occur? If so, what's the consent model?
[06:06] Priya Kapoor: Only if a customer opts in for a specific program or support case. It requires explicit customer consent and is time-limited; we retain evidence of consent in the ticket.

[06:15] Jordan Lee: About model snapshots and logs - if we pin a model and you push a new version, do we get retroactive changes?
[06:21] Priya Kapoor: No. Model variants are immutable for a pinned version; rollouts are opt-in and can be A/B or canaryed. Rolling a new public model won't change your pinned artifact.

[06:30] Luis Ortega: Pen tests and vulnerability disclosures - will you share SOC pen test results or are those redact?
[06:36] Alex Chen: We'll share executive summaries and redacted pen test reports; for deeper artifacts we can set an NDA. We also publish responsible disclosure contacts and timelines.

[06:44] Priya Kapoor: Quick demo note: for the KMS integration we can set up a test tenant where your KMS is used and show key usage logs. That will be part of the technical deep dive.

[06:55] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. On the "anonymized telemetry" you mentioned earlier - can you confirm that telemetry does not include raw prompts or PII?
[07:02] Alex Chen: Confirmed. Telemetry is aggregated and excludes raw prompt text. We use token counts, latency buckets and error surface metrics. Any sampling for diagnostics is subject to customer approval.

[07:12] Dr. Sara Martin: For contract language, Aisha and I will need the exact phrase: "Redwood will not use customer-provided content, prompts or outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any model weights or public models."
[07:25] Alex Chen: We'll provide that exact phrasing and can add definitions for content and derived features.

[07:32] Aisha Khan: Also need the retention default numbers in the contract - default hosted 30 days, extended available, and option for no retention in Dedicated/Private.
[07:40] Maya Lopez: We'll include those numbers in the annex and a small table for retention/region/encryption modes.

[07:46] Luis Ortega: Can we get a timeline for the pilot? We would like a tenant up with EU residency and KMS by ~2026-04-13.
[07:53] Priya Kapoor: That's feasible. We'll need your KMS details (ARNs) and an admin contact to provision.

[07:58] Jordan Lee: Any mention of costs for extended log retention or Private? We'll need rough numbers for procurement.
[08:03] Alex Chen: We'll surface a pricing deck - Maya will follow up. Extended retention and private tenancy are add-ons and we'll include estimates.

[08:11] Dr. Sara Martin: Last question: for compliance evidence, do you provide SIEM integration and automated audit exports?
[08:16] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support direct log export to S3, Splunk, Datadog, or your SIEM. We can also provide scheduled exports of audit logs for compliance.

[08:24] Alex Chen: OK to wrap up - quick recap of commitments and next steps. Alex will send SOC 2 + ISO docs and explicit no-training clause. Priya will schedule the technical deep dive and spin up a EU tenant with customer-managed KMS for bench tests. Maya will send security whitepaper, retention matrix, and pricing deck. Luis will share the list of artifacts you need for procurement.

[08:44] Jordan Lee: Perfect thank you. We'll review and follow up - expect a legal list of contract asks by Friday.
[08:49] Aisha Khan: Thanks all. Appreciate transparency on the no-training and KMS options.

[08:53] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and set the deep dive calendar invite.

[08:58] END
